title: Abba, Father (Galatians 4:1–7)
hookLine: no longer a slave but a child and heir
tomorrow: what does a wooden yoke have to do with being free?

cards: "We're all God's children." It's on mugs, in songs, at funerals. Then Paul writes that God sent his Son "That we might receive the adoption of sons."
Adoption. Nobody adopts a child who's already theirs. It's exactly the kind of thing a kid asks at dinner, about a friend who doesn't go to church.
So which is it: is every person a child of God, or is it a family you're brought into? Christians give two honest answers, and both come from the Bible. Here they are, side by side, each at its best.

teach.b: The first answer: every human being is God's child by being made. In Athens, Acts has Paul quote a Greek poet to a crowd who didn't share his faith: "For we are also his offspring."

teach.h: HAVE WE NOT ALL ONE FATHER?
teach.b: The prophet Malachi asks, "Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us?" On this reading, every face on the street is family before anyone believes anything.
The second answer: in Galatians, child of God names a relationship that's received. Paul pictures an heir who, while small, "differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all."
Then God sends the Spirit "into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father." John's Gospel says the same shape: "to them gave he power to become the sons of God." Become.
On this reading, everyone is made by God and loved, and adoption is the family name, given through Christ. Some readers hold both at once.
Here's one to tell a friend: Abba is an Aramaic word, and Paul doesn't translate it away.
He keeps it and sets the Greek for Father right beside it, the same pair Mark's Gospel puts on Jesus' lips in the garden the night before he died.
Then Paul's conclusion, to each reader: "Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ."

how: Christians pray to God as Father, most often in the Lord's Prayer; Galatians 4:6 and Romans 8:15 are read as the reason they dare to.

o: being brought into a family and given its name
a rule you follow until it becomes a habit
being chosen to lead a congregation

s: abba is a baby word that simply means daddy
a popular claim. Paul sets it right beside the plain word Father, and some scholars warn daddy says too much.
in Acts, Paul quotes a Greek poet to say we are God's offspring
in Athens: as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
Galatians 4 pictures an heir who lives like a servant while small

games.q: you've always heard 'we're all God's children.' a friend asks you to state the adoption view at its strongest. which is it?
o: child of God names a family you're welcomed into, through Christ: Paul says adoption, John says become.
only some people were made by God; the rest were never his at all.
God loves adopted children less than the ones born into the family.
games.why: Galatians 4:5 and John 1:12 speak of receiving and becoming. the other view stands on Acts 17:28 and Malachi 2:10. some readers hold both.

practice: Say two words out loud, once, slowly. If you pray, let them be Paul's: Abba, Father. If you don't, say the name of someone who made you feel like family when you weren't, and let the sound sit in the room.
Then stay quiet with it until the bell.

wordCard.voice: Adoption. Paul's word for being brought into God's family with a family name: no longer a servant, a child and an heir.

orig.note: Greek: adoption. Paul's word in Galatians 4:5, the adoption of sons.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: no longer a slave, but a child who can say Abba. Until tomorrow.
